content: Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir may elevate CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions associated with CYP3A4 substrates. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily. Levoketoconazole also increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Levonorgestrel (intrauterine or oral) increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Maraviroc and lisinopril may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Caution and monitoring are required. Maraviroc increases lofepramine levels or effects by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lonafarnib, a weak P-glycoprotein inhibitor, increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Lopinavir increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Adjust maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily. Loratadine increases maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lorlatinib decreases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mavorixafor increases maraviroc levels via both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised, especially when co-administered with sensitive P-glycoprotein substrates.
